instructions: Peel the potatoes and slice them about 1/8 inch thick. Make them thin, but not so thin that they break when you stir.
Cut the peppers into thin strips and the onion into thin half-moons. Peel the garlic cloves and leave them whole.
Put a very large skillet over medium-low heat and add the olive oil. Add the potatoes, peppers, onion, garlic and 1 tsp of the salt. Stir so everything is coated in oil.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes. The potatoes are done when a fork slides in easily. They should be tender, not browned.
Turn the heat to medium-high and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until some edges turn golden.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of the last 1/4 tsp salt.
method_notes: Everyone agrees on thin potatoes cooked slowly in plenty of olive oil with onion, green and red pepper, and garlic, until tender rather than crisp. Fascinating Spain fries everything in a pan for 20 to 25 minutes and browns it at the end, which is followed here. Searching for Spice simmers it in stock for 40 minutes and Foods and Wines from Spain roasts it for 40 minutes, so those were too slow for a weeknight.
